symptom: a toddler with morning headaches and vomiting
captionSymptom: headaches that kept waking them up at night
hook: the inside of the skull looked like hammered copper
whatYouSee: The whole inner skull vault is covered in rounded scalloped dents like hammered copper.
whyItMatters: The brain is growing inside a skull that cannot expand because its sutures fused too early. The raised pressure presses the brain folds into the inner table and leaves these marks. Untreated it threatens vision and development.
treatment: Surgery releases and reshapes the fused skull to make room for the growing brain. Raised intracranial pressure needs urgent neurosurgical review.
takeaway: Diffuse beaten copper markings with fused sutures in a child point to raised intracranial pressure from craniosynostosis.

findings: Lateral skull radiograph of a child, facing right, including the cervical spine and mandible
Mixed dentition with unerupted permanent tooth buds in the maxilla and mandible, so a young child
Innumerable round, well-defined lucent lesions of fairly uniform size (a few mm to about 1 cm) throughout the calvarium, giving a honeycomb or cobblestone pattern
Lucencies are separated by thin dense bony septa, with a diffuse distribution across the frontal, parietal, occipital and temporal bones
Outer table is thin but appears intact, with no obvious large lytic defect, sclerotic margin or soft-tissue mass
Cranial vault appears relatively large compared with the facial skeleton
Skull base, sella and facial bones are not clearly abnormal on this projection
Cervical vertebrae are visible without evident fracture or malalignment
Soft-tissue shadows at the back and shoulder, with overlying positioning or other external structures
differential: Prominent physiologic digital or convolutional markings with a beaten-copper pattern, as seen with raised intracranial pressure or craniosynostosis, though the diffuse round lucencies are more pronounced than typical
Multiple myeloma-like or metastatic punched-out lytic lesions, such as neuroblastoma metastases or other diffuse lytic marrow disease, including Langerhans cell histiocytosis
Lacunar skull (Luckenschädel) or diffuse osteopenic and fibrous dysplasia-like process
anatomyConcerns: No impossible anatomy identified; the honeycomb pattern is a true diffuse vault abnormality and not a projection artifact
The overlying external soft-tissue density behind the head and neck is likely positioning or support equipment, not pathology
The uniform lucent pattern is unusually regular, so superimposed grid, processing or artifact effect cannot be fully excluded

clueFacts.fact: In craniosynostosis, raised intracranial pressure can be worse after lying flat overnight, so a toddler may often wake up with headaches, and vomiting can also occur in the early morning.
